**THIS IS A DRY RUN**

Quality gate is triggered at https://buildserver.labs.intellij.net/build/939099857 — use this link to get full insight.

Quality gate was triggered with the following revisions:
> **kotlin**
> Branch: `refs/merge/GITHUB-5976/safe-merge`
> Commit: [92e1e44](https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin/commit/92e1e44ef7fb5bd8e8685cb3789af8249ed35a11)

nit: `destination(source, validatePath = false)` still calls `source.relativeTo(this@copyToRecursively)` and `target.resolve(...)`, both of which can throw on their own (`IllegalArgumentException` from `relativeTo` if roots don't match, `InvalidPathException` from `resolve` for names that are valid in the source FS but not in the target FS — e.g. `\0` or `:` when copying from a zip onto a non-Windows / Windows target).

If that happens here, the secondary exception will mask the original one and still bypass `onError` — the same class of bug this PR fixes, in a narrower case.

Two options:
- (a) document this as a known limitation in the comment above, scoping the fix to `IllegalFileNameException` only;
- (b) wrap the resolve in try/catch and fall back to a safe path (e.g. `target.resolve(source.fileName?.toString().orEmpty())` or just `target`) so `onError` always gets called with the original exception.

Either is fine, but currently the comment claims `onError` is now always reachable, which isn't strictly true.

The destination path passed to `onError` is now part of the contract this PR restores — please don't drop it with `_`. Capture and assert at least:

- `source` corresponds to the offending zip entry (e.g. `assertTrue(source.toString().endsWith("test"))`)
- `dst` is the unvalidated resolved path (e.g. `assertFalse(dst.normalize().startsWith(target.normalize()))`)

Without this, a future change that silently re-enables validation inside `error()` would not be caught — the test would still pass as long as the callback is invoked at all (which it would, for some other exception).

Concrete regression this catches:

Suppose someone later "helpfully" clamps `dst` inside `error()` to keep it within `target`:

```kotlin
fun error(source: Path, exception: Exception): FileVisitResult {
    val raw = destination(source, validatePath = false)
    val dst = if (raw.normalize().startsWith(normalizedTarget)) raw else target
    return onError(source, dst, exception).toFileVisitResult()
}
```

Walk-through for the Archive4 entry `../../../../../test`:

1. `destination(source)` at line 237 still throws `IllegalFileNameException` (validation is on at that call site).
2. The `catch` block invokes `error()`.
3. `raw` = `<tmpdir>/UnzipArchive4/../../../../../test` — outside `target`.
4. The new "guard" replaces it: `dst = target`.
5. `onError(source, target, IllegalFileNameException)` is invoked.

The current test passes:
- `failed = true` ✓
- `assertIs<IllegalFileNameException>(exception)` ✓
- `assertTrue(failed)` ✓

…but the restored contract is silently broken — the caller now sees `target` itself instead of the unvalidated path that triggered the error.

The proposed `assertFalse(dst.normalize().startsWith(target.normalize()))` fails here, catching the regression.

> `destination(source, validatePath = false)` still calls `source.relativeTo(this@copyToRecursively)` and `target.resolve(...)`, both of which can throw on their own (`IllegalArgumentException` from `relativeTo` if roots don't match, `InvalidPathException` from `resolve` for names that are valid in the source FS but not in the target FS — e.g. `\0` or `:` when copying from a zip onto a non-Windows / Windows target).

I don't see how we can get an exception from `relativeTo`, but `resolve` can indeed throw one. Not sure if there's a reasonable way to handle it other than updating `onError`'s contract.
